Anna / team — attaching a short technical playbook below, distilled from the checklist, that we typically run for microservice migrations. This is the core incremental approach that minimizes risk: 

- Phase 0 (pre-checks): confirm model pinning, KMS keys, and network egress rules.
- Phase 1 (shadowing): integrate SDK as a secondary client, mirror requests for 48–72h, compare outputs and telemetry.
- Phase 2 (canary): route 5–10% traffic to Redwood with automatic fallback on mismatch.
- Phase 3 (scale): increase in steps while monitoring cost/latency deltas and eval metrics.

Known gotchas relative to HyperscalerX: token-count differences during tokenization-heavy prompts (affects billing estimates), and slightly different default max_output_token truncation heuristics. See the PDF diff.

Proposed quick tests we can run (we can start Monday):
1) Tokenization parity check (subset of 200 prompts).
2) Function-calling JSON fidelity run (20 edge cases).
3) Latency p95 comparison (3 payload sizes).

If you're good, Mina and I can run the 48h probe end-to-end next week.

—Aditya
Applied ML, Redwood Inference

- Tokenization parity: 200 prompts run; 12 prompts had >3 token delta (billing delta estimated +4%). PDF has sample diffs.

- Latency p95: Redwood p95 was 78ms vs HyperscalerX p95 82ms on the same instance class (your recorded traces attached).

Recommended next steps (actionable checklist):
